findings.reason: §2 would build machinery that already exists and §3 lists `--estimated-context` for deletion though it is live and tested, so both sections would be rewritten.
findings.text: the plan's search for existing machinery is incomplete: it cites `reckon/velocity.py:428` `read_sources` and the `reckon/interface_counts.py:575` cache pattern but not `reckon/served_code.py`, whose `_ModuleIndex` (180), `_import_targets` (213), `_module_name` (194), `_module_file` (201) and `_used_definitions` (405) already resolve module names, parse imports and follow attribute references — the exact core `reach.py` proposes to build; and its census of existing usage in §1 calls `reckon crew pick --estimated-context` "used by no skill, test, ledger row, plan or source" when the option is read at `reckon/crew_dispatch_commands.py:600` (definition), `:622` (parameter) and `:693` (passed into `PickRequest`) and consumed at `reckon/crew/picker/snapshot.py:387` and `:708`, with tests exercising it at `tests/test_picker.py:240`

findings.reason: the honest change is to lift the index/closure out of `served_code.py` (or import it) so one owner serves both the served-code report and the reach guard, rather than adding a parallel graph.
findings.text: extend the existing owner rather than fork it: `reckon/reach.py` duplicates `reckon/served_code.py`'s `_ModuleIndex`/`_import_targets`/`_module_name`/`_module_file`/`_used_definitions` (a module index plus an import- and attribute-following worklist that closes transitively over definitions), and it duplicates the qualified-definition enumeration at `reckon/interface_counts.py:74` `definitions()`; a second import-graph core beside the live one drifts from it, and this repository already carries both

findings.reason: §2 must account for the public surface it adds against the current 1626 public definitions, even if only to say the retirements in §3/§4 more than cover it.
findings.text: §2 adds public definitions (`reckon/reach.py`: the production-entry-point reader, the reachable-set result and `neighbourhood`) and does not, in its own text, name what it retires or merges or say why nothing can be; the retirements all sit in §3 and §4, which the section-adding rule does not credit

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — the proposed `reckon/reach.py` hides entry-point resolution, the import graph and the attribute-reference closure behind a reachable-set result and one `neighbourhood(paths)` function; a single module carries the behaviour rather than a spread of shallow wrappers.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — `reckon/reach.py` re-implements the module-index, import-resolution and attribute-reference-closure core that `reckon/served_code.py` already owns, and duplicates the definition-enumeration walk that `reckon/interface_counts.py` already owns. The plan names neither.
rubric_items.interface_budget: a finding — public_definitions 1626, cli_options 351, mcp_views 33, refusal_families 23; §2 adds `reckon/reach.py` (a new module of public definitions) without naming in its own text what it retires or merges, or why nothing can be.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — the plan cites `reckon/velocity.py` `read_sources` and the `reckon/interface_counts.py` cache pattern, but its search for existing machinery missed `reckon/served_code.py` (a live module index that already resolves imports and follows attribute references), and its census of existing *usage* declares `--estimated-context` reached by no source though it is wired through `crew pick` into the picker.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — the plan extends an existing reader (`read_sources`) rather than layering a thin wrapper over it; the added behaviour (entry-point resolution, reach closure) lives in the new module itself, so there is no wrapper lacking justification.
